verses.text: The princes of the people lived in Jerusalem. The rest of the people also cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts in the other cities.
The people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem.

Now these are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the cities of Judah everyone lived in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the children of Solomon’s servants.

Some of the children of Judah and of the children of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. Of the children of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, of the children of Perez;
and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Colhozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.
All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were four hundred sixty-eight valiant men.
These are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah.
After him Gabbai, Sallai, nine hundred twenty-eight.
Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer; and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city.
Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,
Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of God’s house,

and their brothers who did the work of the house, eight hundred twenty-two; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah,
and his brothers, chiefs of fathers’ households, two hundred forty-two; and Amashsai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,
and their brothers, mighty men of valor, one hundred twenty-eight; and their overseer was Zabdiel, the son of Haggedolim.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;
and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who had the oversight of the outward business of God’s house;

and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who was the chief to begin the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brothers; and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred eighty-four.
Moreover the porters, Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates, were one hundred seventy-two.
The residue of Israel, of the priests, the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, everyone in his inheritance.
But the temple servants lived in Ophel: and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple servants.

The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the business of God’s house.
For there was a commandment from the king concerning them, and a settled provision for the singers, as every day required.
Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the children of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people.
As for the villages, with their fields, some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns, in Dibon and its towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
in Jeshua, in Moladah, Beth Pelet,
in Hazar Shual, in Beersheba and its towns,
in Ziklag, in Meconah and in its towns,
in En Rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its towns. So they encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
The children of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija, and at Bethel and its towns,
at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.
Of the Levites, certain divisions in Judah settled in Benjamin’s territory.

footnotes.content: Some cast lots to live in Jerusalem—the holy city. Not by coercion, but by sacred chance. It's the Lord who draws His people to dwell where He dwells, asking only that they be willing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blessing fell on those who offered themselves. We forget this: to step into obedience, even a hard obedience, opens the door to the Lord's benediction. He does not forget volunteers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel, priests, Levites, temple servants, Solomon's servants—all back in the land. A whole community restored. The Lord reassembles His people not as individuals, but as a body with different gifts and callings, all needed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Athaiah, descendant of Perez—and these genealogies trace back to the promises. In naming him, Scripture whispers that the Lord remembers not just individuals, but their lineage, their covenant place in His story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Maaseiah, the son of Baruch—another name linked to God's work (Baruch means 'blessed'). These ordinary lives, recorded in Scripture, remind us that the Lord sees and counts every faithful presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four hundred sixty-eight from Perez—valiant men, all of them named and numbered. The Lord delights in strength that serves His purposes, and He makes it known when His people stand firm.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Benjamin—named carefully, their line preserved. From the tribe that once nearly perished, they returned. God's faithfulness reaches even those whom judgment nearly erased.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nine hundred twenty-eight souls—a remnant of Benjamin restored to the city. Not masses, but faithful numbers. The Lord often works through the small, the true, the committed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joel overseer, Judah second—order restored. As the city breathes again, leadership is appointed. The Lord calls men to steward what He restores, and gives them one another for accountability.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jedaiah the priest—his name means 'Yah knows.' In the restored priesthood, every name speaks of the God they serve. To be called is to be known by the One whose house you tend.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seraiah, ruler of God's house—a weighty title. To oversee the Lord's dwelling requires humility before His presence and careful stewardship of His space. Such men carry a sacred charge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eight hundred twenty-two priests doing the work of the house. Not one priest alone, but a multitude serving together. The Lord's work cannot be done by a solitary hero—it requires a company.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chiefs of fathers' households, two hundred forty-two strong. The old tribal and family order returns. The Lord restores not just individuals to the land, but the whole web of kinship that holds a people together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One hundred twenty-eight mighty men of valor—each counted, each valued. Strength in service to the Lord's house is seen and honored. He misses nothing of what we offer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shemaiah the Levite, his name meaning 'Yah hears.' Even the Levites who lead worship carry names that point their hearts homeward. We are constantly reminded: the Lord listens to His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Levites overseeing the outward business of God's house—the practical work that makes worship possible. Every task done in His service, from the invisible to the seen, is holy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mattaniah led thanksgiving in prayer—his name means 'gift of Yah.' What a role: to stand before the Lord's people and teach them to give Him thanks. He himself is the gift through whom gratitude flows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two hundred eighty-four Levites in Jerusalem. Not a great multitude, but carefully accounted for. The Lord numbers the workers in His harvest, and His eye is ever on their faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Porters keeping watch at the gates—Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers. Humble work, mostly unnoticed, but sacred. Those who stand guard keep the holy place safe. Every faithful vigil is precious to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rest dwelt in their cities, each in his inheritance. The Lord's people return not to Jerusalem alone, but to the whole land restored. His faithfulness reaches everywhere they are scattered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The temple servants lived in Ophel. Once servants of Solomon, now servants in the Lord's house—elevated, restored to purpose. Even the lowly are not forgotten when the kingdom of God is rebuilt.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uzzi, overseer of the Levites, descended from Asaph the singer. Gifts run deep in families—from father to son, the Lord honors the faithfulness of those who seek Him. He builds dynasties of worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A settled provision for the singers, as every day required. The kingdom of God does not forget the singers. He ordains that those who lift His praise shall be cared for. Your worship is not wasted work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pethahiah at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people—a link between earthly government and the Lord's community. Even secular authority touches the life of God's people, and He is not absent from it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Kiriath Arba to Jekabzeel—the land fills again. Names of towns mark the Lord's work rolling across the promised inheritance. Every village, every field, belongs to His design.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeshua, Moladah, Beth Pelet—simple places restored. The Lord cares for the whole tapestry of settlement, not just the great city. His kingdom embraces the small town and the faithful household.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hazar Shual, Beersheba and its towns—the south is repopulated. From Abraham's well to the returned exiles, the Lord's promises endure. Every generation walks the same land in faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ziklag, Meconah—towns where David once dwelt are now restored. What the Lord has given, He holds fast. His people return to inherit what He promised, even after long exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: En Rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth—each name is a place where God's hand has worked through generations. The geography of faith is written in these towns, and the Lord knows each one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom—the full span of restored Judah. Hinnom would later echo with sorrow, yet here it marks the boundary of a reborn people. The Lord encompasses all: redemption and judgment, mercy and truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benjamin settles from Geba onward—the small tribe finds its portion. The Lord assigns each tribe its place with wisdom. He does not overlook the smaller ones; He dignifies every branch of His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah—Benjamin's towns restored. These were places of old, places of priestly memory. The Lord rebuilds not just walls, but the whole inheritance of His people's history.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim—more towns renewed. Each place returns to life. The Lord's work of restoration is not fragmentary; it is thorough, touching every corner where His people dwell.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat—the roll continues. Simple enumeration becomes a love song: the Lord names and claims every place where His covenant people rebuild. Nothing is too small for His remembrance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lod and Ono, the valley of craftsmen—workers settled with their skills. The Lord restores not just leaders and priests, but also the hands that build, weave, and make. All labor in His kingdom is honorable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Levites scattered through Judah and Benjamin—not all in one place. Readers today hear an echo: the Lord's workers serve wherever they are planted, and He multiplies His presence by spreading His people. We need not all gather in one city to be His kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
